shadow:
There is a tightness that has nothing to do with the day. It sits under the breath, around the chest, low in the belly. The breath does not go all the way down. It stops short, and a person learns the shortened breath so early they never knew there was a longer one.

This is what fear feels like once it has settled in for good. Not a thing to point at. A hum in the body that comes with knowing, somewhere, that this all ends. Most people read the hum as a problem to fix, so they spend years braced against it, or numbing it, or staying busy enough that it cannot be heard. The bracing tightens the very thing it fights.

Constriction also turns outward, as gripping. Holding a person too close, holding objects, holding opinions, sure that if the grip ever loosened everything would scatter. The strange part is that the wound has a shape, and the shape has a direction. Something wound that tight is wound around a center, and what is wound can come unwound. The discomfort is not a wall. It is a thread. You follow it inward, which sounds like the last thing you would want to do.
repressive: Some meet the tightness by simply not looking. They keep the wound sealed and call the not-looking peace. The higher feeling dims along with the pain, and a flatness sets in that gets mistaken for who they are.
reactive: Others cannot stand how it feels and aim it outward. They go cold, push warmth away before it lands, because warmth brushes the sore place. Closeness becomes impossible to hold, and the people nearest take the brunt.
gift:
Something loosens when a person stops running and turns toward the tight place instead. Not to fix it. Just to feel it, as a sensation in the body and nothing more. The fear was only ever afraid of being met. Met, it begins to soften.

This is acceptance, and it moves in stages. First you let the body feel what it feels, without arguing. The body is honest in a way the mind is not. Then the breath drops a little lower on its own, and feelings that were locked off come back into reach, and you can hold them without going under.

It helps to know what this is not. It is not the slumped kind of giving up, deciding nothing will ever change. That is just surrender to the tightness. Real acceptance keeps its head up. It looks straight at the wound and says, I see you, and you are not the whole story. There is almost a defiance in it. As the layers relax, love starts moving through a person again where the grip used to be. They stop holding so hard. They stop judging so fast. They feel at home most places, carrying something that has not quite explained itself yet.
siddhi:
Far enough in, the holding is simply gone. There is no one left clutching, because there is nothing felt as separate enough to clutch. The wound that drove all the seeking turns out to have been the way in the whole time.

What is left is love, though not the kind that runs between two people across a gap. This love is the gap closed. It is the thing every form is made of and held together by, the quiet behind all of it. Personal love does not vanish. It widens until it has no edge, until you could not say you love one thing more than another.

It has a particular feel. Not the bright burning kind. This is what stays after the burning, a steady knowing in the cells that none of it was ever apart. Each time a person arrives here, some old tightness lifts a little for everyone, far back down the bloodline. The shame that started it, the sense of not being enough, turns out to have been the seed the whole flower grew from.
